findings.title: Suspect-issue PR comments call methods that do not exist on the workflow
findings.body: get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, but _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration, not on PRCommentWorkflow. PRCommentWorkflow is a separate workflow type that holds an integration; it does not gain that staticmethod. GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body also call self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and self.get_environment_info, which were added only on CommitContextIntegration. Generating a merged-PR suspect-issue comment therefore raises AttributeError and the GitHub/GitLab comment workflow fails instead of posting.

findings.title: Issue titles are interpolated into markdown links unsanitized
findings.body: MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE places the issue title inside a markdown link label: [**{title}**]({url}). Issue titles are attacker-controlled error text and are only length-truncated, not escaped. A title containing ](https://evil.example) or a newline closes the link early and can inject extra markdown into the comment the Sentry bot posts on the customer's GitHub/GitLab PR. Environment names are likewise dropped into the comment in backticks with no escaping.

findings.title: Flagged table widgets render an empty table instead of query results
findings.body: When organization feature use-table-widget-visualization is on, WidgetCardChart renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData hardcoded to data: [] and empty meta, ignoring result.data, result.meta, fields, loading, and the dataset field renderer. Dashboard table widgets for that org show a blank grid instead of the widget query. columns={[]} also does not fall back to meta.fields, because TableWidgetVisualization uses columns ?? derivedColumns and an empty array is not nullish.

findings.title: Error context is paired by dict value order, not node id
findings.body: fetch_error_details loads nodestore blobs with get_multi(node_ids) and then zips error_ids with events.values(). get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id; value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, and backends that omit missing keys shift every subsequent pair. The summary sent to Seer can attribute the wrong title, message, and timestamp to an error id, or drop the wrong events via the data is not None filter. Lookups need to be events.get(node_id) for each id. Timestamps are also used raw in gen_request_data comparisons; a non-numeric nodestore timestamp (ISO string) raises TypeError and fails the whole summarize request.

findings.title: Replay error lookup depends on date filters the client never sends
findings.body: Every summarize request now calls get_filter_params and query_replay_instance before building logs, and process_raw_response is given request.query_params.getlist('field'). The replay AI tab requests /summarize/breadcrumbs/ with no start, end, statsPeriod, or field=error_ids. If get_filter_params rejects a missing range, the previously working summary 400s. If it defaults to a recent window, error_ids is empty for replays outside that window, so error context is silently omitted. A Snuba failure also 500s a path that previously only needed recording segments. error_ids must be requested explicitly and the replay's own time range used, not the caller's page filters.

findings.title: Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching
findings.body: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only inside the search filter branch. When searchQuery is empty the function returns sortAttributes(attributes) immediately, so those internal fields stay visible in the default attributes tree. They disappear only after the user types a query, including when the query would otherwise match them. The exclusion needs to run before the early return.

findings.title: Feedback summary ignores environment (and search) page filters
findings.body: useFeedbackSummary requests /feedback-summary/ with only the normalized datetime and selection.projects. The feedback list page is scoped by the page-filter environment selection (and the search box), but those are not sent. With an environment selected, the Seer summary describes all environments in the projects while the list shows one environment, so the summary does not match the data on screen.

findings.title: Feedback list no longer fills the grid cell and will not scroll
findings.body: The list grid area used to be a FluidHeight Container, which constrained height and scrolled the list inside the 1fr row. It is now SummaryListContainer, a flex column with no min-height: 0, overflow: hidden, or height: 100%. Grid items default to min-height: auto, so the column grows with the summary plus the full list instead of staying in the viewport row, and the inner FluidHeight percentage height does not resolve to the leftover space. The feedback list scroll pane breaks once the summary is shown.

findings.title: Attribute key hook returns undefined after a failed fetch
findings.body: The old hook always reduced the response into a TagCollection, so a failed request still yielded {}. The new hook returns useQuery data directly (attributes: isFetching ? previous : data) and dropped retry: false. On error, data is undefined and isFetching is false, so attributes becomes undefined. Explore callers that spread or index attributes (string tags, number tags, has-tag) will throw when the trace-item attributes endpoint fails. Default react-query retry (3) and refetchOnWindowFocus also replace the previous retry: false and refetchOnWindowFocus: false, multiplying load on that endpoint.

findings.title: 60s deadline is too short for a 100-identity SSO refresh batch
findings.body: check_auth_identities now has processing_deadline_duration=60 while check_auth still hands it up to chunk_size (100) identities. Each identity can do an external IdP refresh. check_auth stamps last_synced before enqueueing this task, so if the worker kills the task at 60s the remaining identities are not refreshed and will not be selected again until the next AUTH_CHECK_INTERVAL (about a day). SSO validity checks are skipped for the tail of every oversized batch.

findings.title: AI summary treats an unloaded project as missing
findings.body: Project is resolved with useProjectFromId({project_id: replayRecord?.project_id}), which is undefined both while the project list is still loading and when the project truly does not exist. The new branch returns 'Project not found' whenever project_id is set and project is missing, before the isPending check, and the summarize query stays disabled. Users hit a hard error (at least a flash, or a stuck error if projects never include that id yet) instead of waiting for the project store.

findings.title: Age/timestamp mutual exclusion treats 0 as absent
findings.body: validate_timestamp and validate_age use initial_data.get('age') and initial_data.get('timestamp') as booleans. Reporting API age of 0 (report just generated) and timestamp of 0 are valid integers allowed by the field constraints, but both are falsy, so a report that includes both is accepted. Neither field is required, so a report with neither age nor timestamp also passes even though each spec needs one of them.
